entries.notes: Settings and history - ESC now opens Settings and the complete patch history. Recovered 24 earlier releases from repository history; future releases are also saved to this device. - Chat visibility can be turned off in Settings and is on by default. UI and boss pacing - Shed Heart drops now come from level 7+ areas. - Item tooltips now stay readable above chat for players and spectators. - Choose an existing character or create a named character at startup. Each character keeps separate progress, gear, quests and map discovery. - Minion health bars no longer overlay the spectator inventory and stash. Removed the permanent Emberwatch ground label and increased the act boss respawn timer to ten minutes. Quest props and summons - Fixed quest body clicks being stolen by NPC hit boxes that balloon when their labels cross the camera plane. Removing or replacing a summoning sceptre dismisses its summoned minions. Combat - Death interrupts skills still in their animation or channel. - Axe and hammer strikes now lead with the weapon head. Changing either hand weapon dismisses your minions. - Final boss phase changes, growth, reveal, and attacks, including phase-two snake strikes, now replicate to spectators.

Quest props and summons - Fixed quest body clicks being stolen by NPC hit boxes that balloon when their labels cross the camera plane. Removing or replacing a summoning sceptre dismisses its summoned minions.
Shed Heart controls - Click or tap Shed Hearts to move them like other items. To reawaken the act boss, right-click a heart in your bag, or hold it for one second and release on touch.

The Shepherd - His first-phase charge is much wider and travels farther. - The main quest now opens the Shed Sanctuary: defeat the Shepherd and his final form, Carrion Saint. - His colossal serpent pursues you and leaves a dangerous body along its route. Bait it carefully to keep an escape path. - The act boss drops one of two exclusive poison weapons: Shepherd's Fang (dagger) or Widow's Choir (bow). - The act boss returns after five minutes. Rare Shed Hearts drop from Act I enemies; click one in your bag to reawaken a defeated boss immediately. Waystones reset - Waystone travel has been reset once for every character: visit the areas again to unlock their waystones. Levels, gear, passives and quests are kept.
Waystones reset - Waystone travel has been reset once for every character: visit the areas again to unlock their waystones. Levels, gear, passives and quests are kept.

Quests: the story so far - Every quest line is now a storyline, all leading to the same dark secret in the north. Quests start over for existing characters (levels, gear and waystones are kept). - New people to meet out in the wilds: Tobias the Gravekeeper, in a candle-warded hut in the Haunted Graveyard, and the Emberwatch - a palisade camp deep in the Ashen Ruins with Commander Varek and Seer Ysolde. Monsters won't follow you into either; Varek's quartermaster sells potions and buys loot. - People send you to each other: Maren to Tobias, Tobias back to Maren, Maren on to the Emberwatch, Hale to Bram, Oda to her brother Varek. - Quests ask more than "kill this many": smash bone totems, break Mortis's reliquaries, recover supply caches and lost crates, take badges and journals from fallen scouts (each with its own story), wake three sunstones to melt the ice sealing the way to the Frozen Hollow, and hold a rite at the Ashen Shrine against waves of the Warlord's host. Many of these call an ambush down on you. - What a quest wants you to find shows on the minimap as an orange square. - Captain Hale and Merchant Oda have their own storylines: The Lost Patrol and The Lost Caravan. Hale's bounty board opens after his. - The story ends at a door beneath the ice. What sleeps behind it is still asleep... for now. Bow skills - Four bow skills that roll on bows and quivers: Split Shot (a wide fan of arrows), Piercing Shot (a heavy shot through every enemy in a line), Rain of Arrows (arrows rain down where you aim) and Burning Arrow (fire arrows that burst and can set enemies burning). - They go on Q E R F like other skills, but pressing one toggles it: while it's on, your bow attack is that skill, with its own draw animation. One at a time; press it again to turn it off. A spinning ring marks the one that's on. No mana, no cooldown. - They are attacks: Additional Arrows, attack speed and attack damage all improve them. - They roll at any level from 1 to 10; stronger monsters drop the high levels far more often. - The Short Bow on Haven's benches now carries Split Shot. - New rare stat on bows and quivers: a chance for bow attacks to fire an additional arrow. Other - War Cry rolls on gear twice as often. - The attack square on the skill bar shows an arrow for a bow (or the bow skill that's on) instead of the bow. - The skills list (K) scrolls now that there are more skills than fit on screen.

The Summoner - Minions now fight for real: enemies attack a minion that is nearer than you (and always a Bone Golem close to them), and minions have life of their own (a green bar when hurt). - Minions don't use your own damage, life or Intelligence. Their life and damage come from the summon's level (steeply, level by level) and from new minion stats: Minion Life, Minion Damage, Minion Speed, Minions take less damage. Without investing in them they fall in a few hits - a summoner who wants an army that holds the line has to build for it. - Summon levels: new "+1 to Level of all Summon Skills" and "+1/+2 to Level of Raise Skeletons / Skeleton Mages / Spirit Wolves / Bone Golem" stats on sceptres, grimoires, helmets, gloves, boots, body armour, amulets and rings. "+1 to all Spells" doesn't raise summons. - Raise Skeletons: skeleton warriors now stay until destroyed. At most 2 (one more at levels 7 and 12); casting again at the cap replaces the most battered one. - New summons: Skeleton Mages (hang back and cast bolts, frail), Spirit Wolves (a fast pack for 12 seconds that enemies can't touch) and Bone Golem (a big temporary brute that taunts enemies round it). - New one-handed weapon: the Sceptre. Its blows put Death Mark on what they hit. A Bone Sceptre carrying Raise Skeletons now lies on the benches in Haven at the start (Raise Skeletons is no longer on the starting helmet). - New off-hand: the Grimoire, for a one-handed weapon or empty hand. Its attack is Death Mark, a bolt that marks an enemy: your minions rush it and hit it 30% harder. - Grave Rot, a curse that rolls on grimoires (and now and then helmets): enemies where you aim deal 20% less damage and take 15% more for 6 seconds, more with each level. - A Necromancy cluster on the passive tree, out past Fire Ward between Wisdom and Zeal: minion life and damage, Lord of Bones (+1 to all summons) and four keystones - Bone Legion, Soul Bond, Death's Herald, Spirit Pact. - Two new uniques: The Ossuary Codex (grimoire) and Gravewarden's Rod (sceptre). - Spectators see every minion, with green bars. Other - Teleport rolls on gear twice as often. - Fixed area skills (Frost Nova, Cleave, Chain Lightning...) and melee blows sometimes missing enemies in cluttered places like Haven's plaza.

Spectators - The chat now always draws over everything else for spectators (skill tree, inventory, every other window), and Enter always brings you back to the chat box. - New buttons over the chat (Bag, Character, Tree, Skills) open the player's menus for you, whatever the player has open. - You can close a menu the player opened - just for yourself; it stays open for them, and shows again the next time they open it. First summoner skill: Raise Skeletons - A new bar skill raises two skeleton warriors that follow you and attack enemies nearby for about half a minute (at most 2 at a time, one more at levels 4, 7 and 10). They hit harder with the skill's level, Intelligence and Spell Damage. - It rolls on helmets, amulets and staves, and the starting Iron Helmet carries it at level 1. - Early version: enemies don't fight back against the skeletons yet, and spectators can't see them yet.

Spectators - The chat now always draws over everything else for spectators (skill tree, inventory, every other window), and Enter always brings you back to the chat box. - New buttons over the chat (Bag, Character, Tree, Skills) open the player's menus for you, whatever the player has open. - You can close a menu the player opened - just for yourself; it stays open for them, and shows again the next time they open it.

A much bigger passive tree - The tree has grown from 25 passives to 94, in six sectors: Might, Grace and Wisdom, and between them three new hybrids - Fury (attacks, critical strikes, Onslaught), Storm (lightning and cold, cast speed, cooldowns) and Zeal (fire, burning, regeneration). - Each sector has its own shape - a wheel, a figure of eight, a long loop, a spiral, a trident, a star with a crown - and bridges join neighbouring sectors at the rim, so a build can cut across instead of walking back to the centre. - Devotion passives grow with every passive you take in their own sector: going deep pays off more than taking a bit of everything. - 14 keystones, several of them tying skills together: Glacial Step (Dash ends in a Frost Nova), Second Wind (War Cry refills mana and extends Onslaught), Stormblade (attack crits arc lightning), Thunderlord (shock), Frostbite (chilled enemies shatter), Avatar of Fire (corpses explode, but other elements weaken), Pain Attunement, Relentless and more. - New effects: critical strikes, ignite (burning), shock (enemies take 25% more damage), shatter, corpse explosions, Onslaught (faster attacks, casts and movement), fire/cold/lightning damage, damage against chilled enemies, damage on low life, % life and mana, % life regeneration, mana on kill. - The tree now fills the screen: drag to look around, scroll (or +/-) to zoom, Centre to fit it all. - Your passives were kept where they still exist; any that moved come back as points to spend. New skill: Teleport - Rolls on amulets, rings and gloves. Blink to where you aim, up to half a screen away, straight through walls and trees. Costs a lot of mana but is ready again almost at once. Harder fights - Armour and Evasion Rating protect much less than before. - Ordinary enemies hit three times as hard, bosses twice as hard. Updates - When a new version goes live you get a 10-second countdown (with a Reload now button) before the page reloads, so you can get somewhere safe first. Your character is saved either way. - Press H to hide the list of controls (and the how-to line on the passive tree); it stays hidden until you show it again. Fixes - Item tooltips grow to fit their text, so long stat lines no longer spill out of the box.

Bosses at double speed - Bosses now do everything twice as fast: they walk twice as fast, swing twice as fast, and every big move winds up and recovers in half the time. - Bosses leap after you on their own, much shorter timer whenever you get out of reach, and land where you're heading rather than where you were.

Mana - Spells cost far more mana as they level up (+40% per skill level): casting nonstop now empties your mana in about ten seconds unless you have mana regeneration gear. Bring mana potions. Updates - When a new version of the game goes live, the page saves your character and reloads onto it by itself within about a minute. Spectators - Bolts, shards and arrows now stop and burst on the monsters they hit, instead of flying straight through them. Items - Items from older versions are brought up to date when you log in: a stat that can no longer appear on that item is removed, values outside today's range are brought into it, a doubled stat keeps one line, and uniques get their current stats. - Item levels top out at 20 (traders stocked better than anything that drops for high-level characters). Fixes - Clicking the stash or a trader no longer picks up whatever item the window opens under your cursor.

Projectiles - Projectiles fired together now hit each target only once: Ice Shard's fan, extra arrows, extra Fire Bolts (and their bursts). The first one to reach an enemy hurts it, the rest pass it by. Spread shots are for crowds now, not for stacking on one enemy. - Ice Shard's shards hit harder to make up for it. - Monster archers' three-arrow volleys hurt you once at most. Items - An item never rolls a stat it already has: no extra Armour on a plate helm, no second life line on a belt. Spells nerfed hard - Spell damage is much lower: base damage cut by about 40%, and each skill level adds 35% instead of 75% (a level 10 spell does about 4x a level 1, not 7.75x). - Intelligence adds 0.6% spell damage per point (was 1.2%). Spell Damage on staves and jewellery is roughly halved. - Fire Bolt's burst is smaller and splashes for less; Chain Lightning loses more damage with each arc. Staff spells cast a little slower. World - The charred woods round the Ashen Ruins (and the dead woods of the Graveyard) are much thicker, with rubble between the trees, so it's clear you can't walk through. Bosses are deadlier - Bosses move as fast as you (Rimeheart faster), hit about 40% harder and attack about 50% faster. - Their big moves come more often and wind up much faster, cover more ground, and aim where you're heading: leaps land past where you're running, the Warlord's fissure follows your path, and falling fire and ice lead you.

Loot - Monsters drop gear about half as often (bosses still always drop theirs). Gold and potions are unchanged. Spell balance - Spells cost more mana (and 15% more per skill level), recover a little slower and hit a little less hard, especially at high levels. Intelligence adds a bit less spell damage. - Mana regenerates more slowly from a large mana pool. Casting nonstop now drains your mana: bring mana potions. Spectators - Spectators now see your spells: staff bolts and shards, Chain Lightning, Frost Nova, Cleave, Dash and War Cry. The bosses, reworked - Gravelord Mortis now wields a huge executioner's axe: he leaps across the crypt and buries it where you stand, whirls it all round himself, and raises the dead. - The Ashen Warlord swings a two-handed maul: he slams it down and the ground cracks open towards you in a line of fire, quake-leaps onto you, and rains fire. - Rimeheart is now a giant frost spider, queen of the ice crawlers: she pounces, bursts frost all round her (it chills), hatches her brood, and calls down ice. - Every big move glows on the ground before it lands. At half life each boss roars into a second phase and attacks faster. - Heavy blows now shake the screen. Two-handed weapons - New weapons: greatswords, greataxes and mauls. They take both hands (no shield), swing slower, but hit far harder, reach further and sweep a wider arc. - The greatsword sweeps wide from side to side, the greataxe chops down from overhead, and the maul is hauled over the head and slammed into the ground with a jolt. - Equipping a two-handed weapon (or a bow) puts your shield back in your bag if there's room. More item variety - Every kind of gear now has lines for Strength (heavy plate and gauntlets), Dexterity (leather and hoods) and Intelligence (silk robes, circlets, sashes), each with four tiers. - Deeper areas and tougher monsters drop the newer tiers much more often; the early ones fade out as you go. - Gear made for a kind of character rolls that kind's stats more often: a silk robe tends to roll mana and Intelligence, plate rolls Strength and Armour. - New bases: bucklers, kite shields, leather belts, cloth sashes, moonstone rings (mana), amber amulets (Strength), and higher tiers of every ring and amulet. - New random stats: life regeneration on armour and jewellery, life leech on melee weapons, gloves and rings, and life on kill on attack weapons, gloves, rings and quivers.

Skills now come from gear - You no longer learn skills by levelling. Every skill is found on gear instead, at a level from 1 to 10, and a higher level hits harder, costs a little more and comes back sooner. - New weapon: staves (two-handed). Every staff carries a spell that becomes your attack: left click (or the aim stick) casts it instead of swinging. Out of mana, you swing the staff instead. - Staff spells: Fire Bolt, Chain Lightning and the new Ice Shard, which flings three chilling shards in a narrow fan. - Staves roll caster stats: spell damage, cast speed, mana, mana regeneration, area of effect, "+1 to level of spells", and now and then a second skill. - Other skills roll where they fit: Cleave on melee weapons, Dash on boots, Frost Nova on helmets and gloves, War Cry on amulets and belts. - New stats: "+1 to Level of all Spells" on amulets, "+1 to Level of all Fire/Cold/Lightning Spells" on rings and amulets, Cast Speed on jewellery and other gear. - Tougher monsters in later areas drop higher-level skills. - A Gnarled Staff with Fire Bolt now lies on the benches in Haven, and the starting boots carry Dash. - Characters from before this change find a staff with Fire Bolt in their bag. Controls - The skill bar has eight slots: Q, E, R, F, and the right, middle and two side mouse buttons. The square on its left shows your attack. - The skills panel (K) shows each skill's level and which item it comes from. - Bow shots, spells and melee swings now go wherever you are aiming at the moment they leave your hand, not where you aimed when you started. Balance - Life and mana regenerate more slowly. - Enraged monsters are much faster, attack 50% faster, and lead their shots and aimed spells to where you are heading. - A monster you kill from a distance no longer flashes "ENRAGED" as it dies. Gear - A Short Bow now lies on the benches in Haven with the rest of the starting gear. - Cleave needs a melee weapon: it can no longer be used with a bow. - New stat: Melee Range, found on gloves and weapons and on the Brute Force passive. - Area of Effect can now roll on amulets and helmets, and the Arcane Mind passive grants it. Bosses - A slain boss returns after two minutes, but only once you are well away from its lair. Interface - The inventory, stash/trader and character windows have an X button to close them. - The character page now shows above the level/life/mana panel instead of under it. Monsters - New creatures roam the wilds: giant spiders, dire wolf packs and bog slimes in Greenwood; grave bat swarms, corpse oozes and crypt spiders in the Graveyard; magma beetles and hellhound packs in the Ashen Ruins; frost wolves and ice crawlers in the Frozen Hollow. - Slimes and oozes burst into smaller ones when killed. - Spiders, wolves and slimes leap at you, aiming where you are heading: a glow on the ground shows where they will land, and anyone in their path is hit too. - Every creature has its own sounds, movement and death. - Humanoid monsters (and you) now breathe while standing still and put their whole body into each swing. - Monsters move faster, and keep chasing you much further. - Hit a monster from a distance and it may become enraged for a few seconds: much faster, hitting harder and attacking quicker. - Small creatures like slimelings can now be hit by arrows, spells and melee. - The minimap spots monsters further away, even in ground you haven't explored yet. World - Removed the gate in the Ashen Ruins that led straight back to Haven; use the town portal or a waystone to go home.

Minimap - The minimap no longer gives away gates, the waystone or townsfolk you haven't discovered yet. - Monsters only show on the minimap when they are close by. Spectating - Spectators now see the player's inventory, stash/trader, character page, passive tree and skills panel when the player opens them, and the stats of whatever item the player points at. Move your own mouse to look around yourself; after a moment it goes back to following the player. Spectators can also open these (I, C, P, K) on their own. World - Rivers (and lava/frozen rivers) now have raised banks instead of floating flat on the grass, so it's clear you can't walk into them; rivers also flow.

Fixes - Fixed a bug from the last update that broke dragging items in the inventory on phones. - While dragging an item, its stats now stay on screen the whole time; hovering another item while dragging shows both items' stats side by side. - Gold pickup sound is much quieter again. - Gold autocollects from twice as far away. - Enemies now aggro if you shoot them from far away, and nearby enemies wake up too when one of them aggroes. - Rivers (and lava/frozen rivers) now have raised banks instead of floating flat on the grass, so it's clear you can't walk into them; rivers also flow.

Phones - Much bigger mobile performance push: shadows are now off entirely on phones, render resolution is a bit lower, and lighting is simplified (fewer lights, simpler shading). Mobile trades looks for frame rate; PC is untouched. - The passive skill tree no longer gets cut off top and bottom on phones. Fixes - Gold pickup sound (not just the drop sound) is much quieter. - Player's own light is bigger and brighter, so nearby things are easier to see in the dark.

Fixes - Menus (inventory, character page, stash/trading) no longer let a click through to an NPC standing behind them. - Clicking an NPC now requires already being reasonably close to them, so an accidental click on a distant/background NPC won't send you walking across the map. - Performance: only your current area simulates its enemies now (other areas used to keep running in the background the whole time); mobile rendering was also tuned down (antialiasing, shadow quality), which should help frame rate noticeably, especially on phones.

Phones - Attacking and casting now use a second stick (where the attack button used to be) instead of a button: drag it to aim, hold it off centre to keep attacking or casting that way. Works the same for melee, bows and spells - there's no more auto-aim, so you're always in control of the direction. Fixes - Gold dropping on the ground is much quieter. - Items on the ground are easier to click or tap - the target around them is bigger than the icon itself.

Fixes - An item's stats no longer stay stuck on screen after you pick it up. - Phones: the chat opens over the minimap and quest tracker instead of under them. - Phones: holding the attack button with nothing in reach now attacks the way the joystick points (before, you kept facing wherever your first swing went). - Phones: Haven runs faster (fewer lights drawn at once, lighter shadows). - Spectators stay closer to live on slow connections: the server skips frames instead of queueing seconds of them. - Spectators can see whether the player they watch is on a phone or a PC. - Putting a weapon down no longer rings like a doorbell. - Phones: the stash and trade panels no longer overlap your equipment and bag. - iPhone: the game no longer gets pillarboxed with black bars on the sides in landscape. Sounds - Armour, belts and quivers make their old pickup sounds again; swords, axes and maces clang, bows knock like wood. Item sounds are all about equally loud now. Haven - A stash chest stands by the market stalls: click it to store items (12x12). Ctrl+click moves an item straight between your bag and the stash. It's saved with your character. - Clicking inside the open inventory no longer swings your weapon at the world behind it. Uniques and keystones - New special stats that change how you play: extra arrows, extra Fire Bolts, spell damage, area of effect, life regeneration, mana regeneration, life leech, Mind over Matter, extra Chain Lightning arcs, chill on hit, Culling Strike and life on kill. - Every unique now has at least one: Whisperwind fires 3 arrows, Bonehew leeches life, Ashfall culls, Emberheart boosts spells, Elder's Charm adds a lightning arc, and more. - Six new uniques: Rimefletch, Leechfang, Twinflame Loop, Stormcaller's Circlet, Bloodroot Cord and Mantle of the Still Mind. - Each arm of the passive tree now ends in a keystone (the diamonds): Executioner, Bloodthirst, Frostbite, Volley, Twin Casting and Mind over Matter. - Life now regenerates very slowly on its own. Everyone takes 10% of hits from mana (was 30%); Mind over Matter and some gear add more. - The character page lists your special stats. Minimap - The minimap now shows the ground: open paths, trees, rocks, walls and dead ends, with a grainy texture in each area's colour. - Fog of war: you only see the parts you've explored, and that's remembered with your character. Monsters show only nearby, in explored ground. Potions and gold - Gold now drops on the ground: walk over it (or click it) to pick it up. - Potions drop on the ground too. They go into two potion slots in your inventory, next to your body armour: only potions fit there, they stack up to 10, and they can't be sold. Click a slot (or press 1 / 2) to drink. Trading - Oda and Bram now trade properly: their goods appear beside your bag. Click an item to buy it; Ctrl+click an item in your bag (or drop it on their side) to sell it. Prices show on the tooltips, and what you sell can be bought back. - Their stock fits your level and restocks as you grow or after a while. - Bram still gambles, now for more gold but with better odds: rare or better half the time, and sometimes a unique.

Fixes - Shadows no longer come and go as you move: the browser version only drew them up to 30 m from the camera, which ended right around your character. They now reach 65 m. - This window no longer opens underneath the name prompt. Interface - Click a skill square on the bar to pick which skill goes there (or empty it). K still opens the full skill list.

Fixes - Casting Chain Lightning or Fire Bolt with a bow no longer also shoots an arrow (and with a melee weapon no longer adds a free swing). - Clicking an item to pick it up no longer swings at the air on the same click. - Clicking a townsperson or a waystone is more forgiving (their name tag counts too), and never shoots them. - Clicking a gate walks you through it. - Haven is listed first on the waystone. - Right-clicking in the game no longer opens the browser menu in Firefox. - Bows re-aim at the target when the arrow leaves, so shooting while strafing hits what you clicked. Arrows also hit enemies they visibly graze. Loot - Each rarity has its own drop sound; uniques ring out. (The odd thud when an enemy died was the old item-drop sound.) - Picking up and putting down items sounds like what they are: weapons clink, armour thumps, jewellery glimmers. - Item base stats now vary a little (a 15 Evasion Rating base rolls 12 to 16). - Items dropping on the same spot spread out so every icon shows, and items and their names draw over corpses. - Hover an item on the ground to see its stats; hovering items while holding one shows their stats too. - Bows and quivers drop much more often, and there's a new early Crude Bow. - More caster and archer gear: Silk Robe, Silk Gloves, Silk Slippers, Sage Circlet, Hunter Hood, Mystic Robe; Intelligence and Dexterity roll on more slots. Balance - Spells gain 1.5% damage per Intelligence (was 2%). - Chain Lightning reaches 9 m (was 12) and rewards aim: cast on an enemy under the cursor for full damage (+25% up close); a blind cast hits for 70%. Each arc deals 70% of the one before. Interface - A pulsing note above the skill bar shows when you have passive points to spend (click it or press P). - The chat sits under the inventory and its tooltips. When you're not typing its background disappears and messages fade after a while; scroll the mouse wheel over it to read back. - A soft white light around your character keeps nearby things readable in the dark. - This window: a note of what changed, once per update.
